UX Bug: "Help" displays onHover(), but with a delay. So I click on the help button, but nothing appears. In reality, here is what is happening:
onHover(): "Oh, I see that you want me to show you the tooltip. Hang on for about 250ms"
onClick() after about 100ms: "Oh, I was going to show you the tooltip, but you clicked, which tells me that you want to turn the tooltip off. OK. I won't show you anything."

Solution: Please just display help tooltips onClick(), instead of onHover(). Clicking again anywhere should toggle the tooltip off.

Feedback from an emergency manager:
For reports, I think a visual of the reported damage areas as a PDF, graphs of those who have been helped vs needing help vs registered and agencies that have assisted, spreadsheet data dumps with being able to filter by who still needs help, and number of volunteer hours – all that would be great by email. A daily snapshot with number of people registered, number of people assisted, number of people needing help, number of agencies involved, and number of volunteer hours recorded by text would be phenomenal.

Feedback from a volunteer:
Being able to easily see a list in a geographic area that is claimed or who has not been contacted yet in an easy to read PDF would be wonderful.  Also having it automatically send to include new cases to my email would be wonderful.

Feedback from a volunteer:
Graphs would be best for me to my email!

Another example from a volunteer:
![Example of Reports Dashboard](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4184619/84444427-fd6c5680-abfe-11ea-81ac-7edf88a77115.png)

Feedback from another volunteer:
I like the ability to download the data into a spreadsheet and then sort & filter as needed.  I like the ability to just go get it when I need it, no need to send it periodically or anything like that.  I could see the benefit of charts & graphs, as some folks are more visual like that than others.  Perhaps having that as the display (number of hours worked, number of work orders and their particular status, etc.) but have the ability to download it into an excel file as an option.

I just don't see the value of PDFs, unless it is a colorful graph or bar chart.

Feedback from another volunteer:
The only thing I have had to deal with is volunteer hours and a spreadsheet format is fine.

Per Tobi, this is not a problem because Django will automatically interpret a string number as an integer. Just use an integer both ways, and it should be fine.

```
UPDATE worksite_worksites_work_types_statuses_phases AS wwwtsp
SET case_number_suffix = 'A'
WHERE wwwtsp.case_number_suffix IS NULL
AND wwwtsp.incident_id IS NULL
AND wwwtsp.work_type_claimed_by IS NOT NULL;
--12

UPDATE worksite_worksites_work_types_statuses_phases AS wwwtsp
SET incident_id = ww.incident_id, phase_id = 4
FROM worksite_worksites AS ww
WHERE wwwtsp.worksite_id = ww.id
AND wwwtsp.incident_id IS NULL;
--214

UPDATE worksite_wwtsp AS wwwtsp
SET incident_id = ww.incident_id, phase_id = 4
FROM worksite_worksites AS ww
WHERE wwwtsp.worksite_id = ww.id
AND wwwtsp.incident_id IS NULL;
--216

```

Include phone users that match this criteria:
```
-- Since a particular date
SELECT uu.first_name, uu.last_name, uu.email, uu.mobile, oo.name AS organization_name
FROM user_users AS uu
LEFT JOIN phone_dnis_statuses AS pds
ON uu.id = pds.created_by
LEFT JOIN organization_organizations AS oo
ON uu.organization_id = oo.id
WHERE uu.id IN(
  SELECT DISTINCT(created_by)
  FROM phone_dnis_statuses
  WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
)
AND pds.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
GROUP BY uu.first_name, uu.last_name, uu.email, uu.mobile, oo.name
ORDER BY uu.last_name, uu.first_name;
```
